title: Mondo Enduro
who: Austin Vince, Gerald Vince, Chas Penty and friends

media.title: Mondo Enduro
media.note: The expedition film, shown on Discovery

media.title: Terra Circa
media.note: Austin Vince's 2001 sequel, back to the Zilov Gap

summary: A group of friends from a London school staff room go round the world the longest way in the shortest time, on cheap Suzuki DR350s, rough camping on a shoestring: across Central Asia and Siberia through the roadless Zilov Gap to Magadan, from Alaska to Chile, and up Africa from Cape Town home to London. Their film became a cult classic of adventure riding.

sources.label: Adventure Motorcycle: riders getting candid with Austin Vince

approximate: Places from the film's chapter list; the roads between them are the router's choice and only approximate.

stops.text: East along the half-built highway across Siberia.

stops.name: Irkutsk
stops.text: By Lake Baikal; three riders head home here.

stops.name: Zilov Gap
stops.text: The roadless Zilov Gap: bogs, rivers and broken bikes. Austin Vince later called it the best ten days of the whole trip.

stops.name: Skovorodino
stops.text: Exhausted, they took the Trans-Siberian train for the last 100 miles of the gap.

stops.name: Yakutsk
stops.text: North to the Lena river: no road onwards then.

stops.name: Khandyga
stops.text: A river barge down the Lena to where the road starts again.

stops.name: Magadan
stops.text: The Road of Bones to the Pacific, 111 days after leaving London.

stops.name: Anchorage
stops.text: Bikes and riders flown to Alaska: good roads and full shops, a culture shock.

stops.name: San Francisco
stops.text: Another rider has to leave, out of money; three carry on.

stops.text: The end of the road north of the Darién Gap.
